title: Writing: A Discursive Essay on Justice and Reform

writingModel.placeholder: Introduce the justice issue and present both perspectives
writingModel.hint: Use modal passives: "Citizens must be protected by law / are entitled to equal justice"

writingModel.placeholder: Case for reform — evidence of injustice in the current system
writingModel.hint: Use formal modals: "Defendants are required to… / are prohibited from… / must be…"

writingModel.placeholder: Counter-argument — why the current system has value
Specific reform proposals — what must / should / shall change
writingModel.hint: "Legal aid must be substantially increased." / "Courts shall be required to…"

writingModel.placeholder: Balanced conclusion — what a just system is obliged to provide
writingModel.hint: "A just society is obliged to guarantee… / Citizens are entitled to…"

writingTemplate.prefix: Access to justice is a fundamental right to which
writingTemplate.placeholder: all citizens are entitled, regardless of their financial means
writingTemplate.hint: "Are entitled to" = have the right to (start with a rights claim)

writingTemplate.prefix: However, in practice, those without financial resources are often
writingTemplate.placeholder: prohibited from accessing high-quality legal representation
writingTemplate.hint: "Prohibited from" or "denied access to" — show the gap between right and reality

writingTemplate.prefix: Defenders of the current system argue that defendants
writingTemplate.placeholder: are required to accept some inequality as a consequence of individual freedom
writingTemplate.hint: Fairly present the counter-argument using formal modals

writingTemplate.prefix: Nevertheless, it is clear that fundamental reforms
writingTemplate.placeholder: must be introduced to ensure that justice is equally accessible
writingTemplate.hint: "Must be introduced" = modal passive obligation for reform

writingTemplate.prefix: In a truly just society, no citizen
writingTemplate.suffix: , and all are entitled to the full protection of the law.
writingTemplate.placeholder: must be denied access to justice on the grounds of poverty
writingTemplate.hint: "Must be denied" = modal passive prohibition — this must not happen

items: All citizens are entitled to equal protection under the law.
Defendants are entitled to a fair trial, regardless of their background.
Citizens are entitled to know the charges brought against them.
Those who cannot afford legal representation are entitled to legal aid.
Every individual is entitled to be presumed innocent until proven guilty.
States are required to provide legal aid to those who cannot afford representation.
Courts are obliged to treat all parties equally before the law.
Governments are required to reform institutions that perpetuate inequality.
Lawyers are obliged to maintain the confidentiality of client communications.
Judges are required to declare conflicts of interest before hearing a case.
Police are prohibited from conducting searches without a valid warrant.
Suspects must not be questioned without access to legal advice.
Confessions may not be obtained through coercion or duress.
Evidence may not be withheld from the defence team.
Juvenile offenders shall not be tried in adult courts.
Legal aid must be substantially increased to address structural inequality.
All parties shall be entitled to timely hearings without undue delay.
Courts shall be required to monitor and report on demographic inequalities in outcomes.
Restorative justice programmes should be made available in all criminal cases.
Independent oversight of the police must be established and fully resourced.

questions.text: "All citizens ___ ___ equal access to the justice system." (= have the right to)
questions.hint: "Are entitled to + noun" = have the legal right to

questions.text: "Suspects ___ ___ of their right to remain silent before questioning." (must — passive obligation)
"Governments ___ ___ to reform legal aid systems — it is a legal obligation." (formal)
questions.hint: "Are required to + infinitive" = formal external obligation

questions.text: "Evidence ___ not ___ from the defence team under any circumstances." (may — passive prohibition)
questions.hint: "May not be + pp" = formal passive prohibition

questions.text: "Police ___ ___ conducting searches without a valid judicial warrant." (formal prohibition)
questions.hint: "Are prohibited from + gerund" = formal written prohibition

questions.text: "Are entitled to" expresses a right, while "are required to" expresses an obligation.
questions.hint: "Entitled to" = right; "required to" = obligation — different directions

questions.text: "In a just society, all parties ___ ___ access to timely and fair judicial proceedings." (shall — written law)
questions.hint: "Shall be + pp" or "shall have" = formal mandatory provision

questions.text: "Restorative justice processes ___ ___ voluntary — participation cannot be mandated." (must — passive)
